newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper stocks may be poised for big jump-trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper stocks may be poised for big jump-trade.

text.p: There was a wide spread of estimates for movements in London Metal Exchange (LME) copper stocks on Tuesday among Asian traders, though the balance of opinion was towards a sharp hike in inventories.
Expectations ranged between a 5,000-15,000 tonnes rise in copper stocks, but the aluminium figures were seen dipping by between 3,000 to 5,000 tonnes.
On Thursday, base metal traders in London estimated an increase of 10-15,000 tonnes in copper, while their New York counterparts predicted a hefty 15,000 to 25,000-tonne jump.
Singapore traders said they were expecting a marginal rise of between 2,000-3,000 tonnes in LME copper stocks in the city-state. Lead and aluminium inventories here were also seen higher, they said.
Three-month LME copper was quoted around $2,155/$2,156 a tonne at 0430 GMT, down slightly from the London close, while cash metal was indicated at $2,368.
Traders said that fund selling was pushing LME copper lower and the backwardation, or cash to three months premium, had narrowed to around $212 down from $250 on Thursday.
"The backwardation will probably narrow further," one said.
Singapore base traders assessed support for three-month metal at between $2,050-$2,100 a tonne.
Three-month LME aluminium was quoted at $1,613/14 a tonne at 0430 GMT, traders said.
